# ECN-2026-036 Change notice - Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L1-SB03

Related documents: SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, SOP-P2-L1-05

## Reason for change
This engineering change notice updates the maintenance specification for the blast wheel liner bolt tightening on Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03). Field inspection and root cause analysis of recurring liner movement identified that inconsistent bolt preload was a contributing factor to premature liner wear and unexpected wheel imbalance. The change standardizes the bolt torque requirement to ensure consistent clamping force, reduce relative motion between liner and adapter, and improve component life and shot quality.

Key drivers:
- Eliminate variable operator practice observed during service records review.
- Reduce unscheduled downtime associated with liner rework and wheel balancing.
- Align the maintenance instruction with bolted-joint best practice for this assembly.

The approved bolt torque value to be applied to the blast wheel liner bolts on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 is 50 N·m. This value supersedes any previous informal guidance and is the new controlled setting for the cabinet.

## Affected items
Primary affected equipment:
- Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03)

Affected maintenance procedures and records:
- Operation and maintenance activities in SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, and SOP-P2-L1-05 where blast wheel liner removal or reinstallation is performed. Technicians must follow the updated torque requirement when reassembling the liner.

Affected personnel:
- Maintenance technicians assigned to P2, line P2-L1
- Shift supervisors overseeing preventive and corrective maintenance on shot blast equipment
- Quality personnel who verify wheel balance and shot pattern after liner service

Note: No changes are made to any other fasteners, sealing interfaces, or structural components beyond the blast wheel liner bolts for EQ-P2-L1-SB03 under this notice.

## Implementation
Scope
- This ECN mandates application of the specified blast wheel liner bolt torque for all maintenance events that involve liner removal and reinstallation on EQ-P2-L1-SB03.

Tools and calibration
- Use a calibrated torque wrench appropriate for the head style of the liner bolts. Calibration status must be verified before use per existing calibration program referenced in SOP-P2-L1-03.

Procedure steps (summary)
- Remove access covers per SOP-P2-L1-03 and expose the blast wheel assembly.
- When reinstalling the liner, hand-start bolts to ensure proper thread engagement and alignment.
- Using a calibrated torque wrench, apply the specified torque to each liner bolt. The required setting is 50 N·m.
- Tighten bolts in a crossing pattern to distribute clamp load evenly and minimize liner distortion.
- After torquing, rotate the wheel by hand to verify free rotation and absence of interference.
- Perform a dynamic check of wheel balance and shot distribution per SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05.

Rationale for steps
- Hand-starting and a crossing pattern reduce the risk of cross-threading and uneven clamping, which directly addresses the root cause of liner micro-motion.
- Applying the controlled torque value provides predictable clamping force across assemblies, reducing variation in wear behavior.
- Rotation and dynamic checks verify that the applied torque yields a functional assembly without binding or imbalance.

Examples and nonconformance handling
- Example: If after torquing at 50 N·m the wheel exhibits unusual resistance during manual rotation, do not return the cabinet to service. Tag out the equipment and notify maintenance supervision for inspection. Record findings on the maintenance work order and follow corrective actions documented in SOP-P2-L1-04.
- Example: If a bolt cannot achieve the specified torque due to thread damage or stripped head, replace the affected fastener and associated captive hardware, then apply the specified torque. Record replacement details on the maintenance record.

Records to keep
- Maintenance work order showing liner removal/reinstallation and confirming application of the specified torque value of 50 N·m for EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
- Torque wrench calibration certificate or sticker indicating current calibration status used for the task; attach or reference calibration ID per SOP-P2-L1-03.
- Post-service quality verification report documenting wheel rotation check and shot pattern verification performed under SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05.
- Any Nonconformance Report created due to inability to achieve the specified torque or detected assembly issues; include disposition and corrective actions taken.

Document updates
- Update the step in SOP-P2-L1-03 that references liner reassembly to cite the new torque requirement for EQ-P2-L1-SB03.
- Add a note in SOP-P2-L1-04 and SOP-P2-L1-05 to reference the torque confirmation as a prerequisite for post-service verification tasks.

Training
- Brief maintenance teams on the change during the next scheduled toolbox meeting. Emphasize the 50 N·m requirement and the importance of using calibrated tools.
- Supervisors to verify the first three applications of the new torque setting on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and sign off on associated records.

## Approvals
Authorized changes under this ECN require sign-off by Maintenance Engineering, Operations, and Quality Assurance. Approval signatures shall be recorded in the ECN approval block and retained with the equipment maintenance file. Once signed, distribute this ECN to maintenance supervisors, shift leads, and the document control system; update SOP-P2-L1-03, SOP-P2-L1-04, and SOP-P2-L1-05 references accordingly.

Document control note
- This ECN becomes the governing instruction for blast wheel liner bolt torque on EQ-P2-L1-SB03 and must be referenced in future revisions of the cited SOPs.
